Rocuronium is an intermediate-acting aminosteroid non-depolarising muscle relaxant

Mechanism: competitive antagonist of nAChR at NMJ

Post-synaptic nAChR antagonism → muscle relaxation

Intubating dose 0.6mg/kg produces paralysis within 60-120s for \~30mins

\>70% receptor occupation required for paralysis

Recovery of neuromuscular function depends on:

a\. Rocuronium at NMJ

b\. PK factors 

b\. PD factors

**Concentration of Rocuronium at NMJ**

- Increasing dose of rocuronium →↑Rocuronium at NMJ →↑time for diffusion back into plasma →↑duration of block 
- Time since administration →↓time since administration →↑ plasma/NMJ Concentration →↑time till recovery 

**PK Factors**

**Distribution**

Singe Bolus dose - ↑ rate of recovery as redistributed 

Repeat dosing - ↓ rate of recovery due to accumulation 

Metabolism: 

\< 5% hepatic metabolism → ↓rate of recovery with: Hepatic dysfunction; hypothermia (↓enzymatic function)

Elimination:

70% hepatic/biliary clearance → longer duration in hepatic dysfunction 

30% renal dysfunction → longer duration in renal dysfunction 

**PD Factors**

**Volatile agents** 

→ Potentiate Blockade 

↑Skeletal muscle blood flow and ↓muscle tone / motor activity from CNS/spinal cord

**Magnesium**

↑Magnesium → Potentiate Blockade

↑Mg2+ → antagonize Ca2+ at L-Ca2+ channel → reduced ACh release 

**Calcium Channel Antagonist** 

→ Potentiate Blockade

↓Ca2+ influx  →↓ACh release 

**Aminoglycosides**: 

→ Potentiate Blockade 

Aminoglycosides →↓Ca2+ influx  →↓ACh release

**Physiological States:**

Elderly → ↓ muscle mass ↓Vd → longer duration 

Pregnancy → ↑ GFR, ↑Vd ↑hepatic enzymatic function → ↑ rate of recovery 

**NMJ Disease:**

Myasthenia Gravis → ↓nAChR → ↑ sensitive to Roc

**Reversal Agents:**

- Anticholinesterases such as neostigmine →↑ ACh at NJM → decrease time to recovery 
- Gamma cyclodextrin (sugammadex)  → forms complex with rocuronium in plasma → concentration gradient to remove roc from NMJ
- reversal action/effectiveness and speed of reversal dependant on depth of blockade when administered (amount of Roc at NMJ) and dose of reversal given
